title: The Fox and the Goat
originalTitle: Greek title not preserved in this edition
sourceAuthor: Aesop; selected and retold by Joseph Jacobs

artLabel: A fox looks up from a well as a curious goat peers over the rim.

pageArt.alt: The Goat leaps into the well after listening to the Fox’s tempting advice.
The Fox springs from the Goat’s horns to the rim while the Goat remains below.

scenes: By an unlucky chance a Fox fell into a deep well from which he could not get out. A Goat passed by shortly afterwards, and asked the Fox what he was doing down there.

“Oh, have you not heard?” said the Fox; “there is going to be a great drought, so I jumped down here in order to be sure to have water by me. Why don’t you come down too?” The Goat thought well of this advice, and jumped down into the well.
But the Fox immediately jumped on her back, and by putting his foot on her long horns managed to jump up to the edge of the well. “Good-bye, friend,” said the Fox, “remember next time,
“Never trust the advice of a man in difficulties.”
